body.statement: Suppose \(C,D\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) are nonempty disjoint convex sets. Then there are \(a\ne0\) and \(b\in\mathbb R\) such that \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) for every \(x\in C\) and \(a^{\mathsf T}x\ge b\) for every \(x\in D\). Conversely, if \(C\) and \(D\) are convex, at least one is open, and such a separating hyperplane exists, then \(C\) and \(D\) are disjoint.

source.locator: Section 2.5.1, separating hyperplane theorem and converse separating hyperplane theorem, printed pages 46 and 50
